StepSettle.title: StepSettle
StepSettle.description:
Settle a running step whose run has submitted (it is finishing) on that submission: its
agent is stopped as a cancel stops it, and the step succeeds with the outputs the done
signal would have given it. Only a bare agent fn's step; anything else is refused.

StepProgress.title: StepProgress
StepProgress.description:
Publish a running step's latest values without finishing it, from its current run. Each
field is one of the step's outputs (its fn's or declared) and is checked against its type;
the fields merge over the run's earlier progress. Progress is never final: it feeds no
input, handoff or gate, settles nothing, writes no log record and wakes no wait.

BoardSet.description:
`board_set`: set the project's board (an OpenUI Lang program, `docs("board")`) or clear it
with a null `program`. A stale `expected_rev` is a conflict, a program that does not check
is invalid (each bad line listed).

program.description: The board program; null clears the board.

BoardDocRead.description: `board_doc_read`: the board's document, the hand-written part a board's `Doc()` draws.

BoardDocWrite.description:
`board_doc_write`: replace the board's whole document. With `expected_rev`, a document
at another revision is a conflict and nothing changes; the same text again changes nothing.

markdown.description: The whole document, as markdown (at most 64 KiB).

expected_rev.description: The document's revision you read (board_doc_read); refused if it has changed since.

BoardDocEdit.description:
`board_doc_edit`: replace line ranges of the board's document at `expected_rev`, all of
them or none.

expected_rev.description:
The document's revision the line numbers come from (board_doc_read); refused if it
has changed since.

edits.description: The edits, by line numbers of that revision; none may overlap another.

DocEdit.description:
One edit of the board's document: lines `start` to `end` (1-based, inclusive) become
`text`. `end = start - 1` inserts before `start`; `start = lines + 1` appends.

text.description: The new lines (several, or "" to delete the range).

rev.description: The revision the edit was worked out from; another current one is `conflict`.

start.description: `false` adds new steps paused (`"paused": true`) unless they set `paused` themselves.

PlanOp.description:
One operation of `plan_edit`. Operations apply in order to one candidate (each sees what
those before it did); the candidate is validated once, whole, and commits all or nothing.

oneOf.description: Declare a plan input or replace its declaration (an existing one keeps its position).
Declare a plan output `{"source": source}` or replace it.
`step` is a step id or `unit:<name>` (that unit's entry steps).

after.description: Recipe step suffix (or `*`, the unit's entry steps) to gate entries.

inputs.description: Recipe step suffix to input name to a literal value.

oneOf.description: Change the unit's member steps, each by its exact id.
Every current member of the collection exactly once, in the new order. Needs `rev`.

StepChanges.description:
A step's fields to change: each given field replaces that field, null removes it, an
absent one is left as it is. `in` replaces the whole binding map. At least one field.

UnitUpdate.description: `unit_update`: change a unit's member steps by their exact ids.

UnitRemove.description: `unit_remove`: remove every step of a unit.

PlanRead.description: `plan_read`: a page of the plan's steps, in `(position, id)` order.

recipe.description: Only the units this recipe matches (SPEC §6.8's dynamic matching).

subtree.description:

a selected step, transitively.

keep.description:

Ask.description:
A question that needs a reply. `to` is a step of the project's current plan,
`orchestrator` or `owner`; the thread and sender are derived, never given.

to.description: Required; a missing or unknown recipient is refused as `invalid`, never stored.

run.description: The asking run: its step is the sender. Without it the caller is the orchestrator.

owner.description: The dashboard speaks as the owner.

Say.description: A note; no reply is expected.

to.description: Required; a missing or unknown recipient is refused as `invalid`, never stored.

Reply.description: A reply to one message: to its sender, on its thread. It resolves an open question.

to_message.description: Select exactly one of this message id or `to`, a sender with one open question.

to.description: Answer this sender's single open question addressed to the caller.

MessagePost.description:
The retired `message_post` wire shape. Only runs started before ask, say and reply
send it; the coordinator translates it and refuses it without a run identity.

owner.description: Read as the owner (the dashboard's identity) instead of the orchestrator.

StepDismiss.description:
The owner sets a cancelled step aside (`dismissed`), or back: a dismissed cancel stays on
its unit but no longer marks its project or holds its unit off the shelf, until the step
is cancelled again. Kept like a read mark (`readers`), never a log record.

LogRead.description:
A page of the log. Every filter narrows only the records it speaks of (an empty list is no
filter): `kinds` every record, `threads` and `recipients` message records, `statuses`
step.status records; a record is kept when every filter that applies to it keeps it.
`threads` without `kinds` also keeps messages only.

statuses.description: Only step.status records whose `to` is one of these.

recipients.description: Only message records whose `to` is one of these (a step id, `orchestrator`, `owner`).

StepWait.description:
`step_wait`: wait until every selected step's status meets `until`, or `timeout_seconds`
pass. Exactly one of `steps` and `tags` selects.

until.description:
`"succeeded"`, `"settled"` or `{"any_of": [statuses]}`. The coordinator checks it and
refuses a bad one as `invalid`.

StepWaitUntil.description:
What `step_wait` waits for: every selected step succeeded, every one settled (§7.1), or
every one in one of the listed statuses.

PlanHistoryQuery.description: `plan_history`: a page of the plan's history, oldest first.

after_seq.description: Only records whose `seq` is greater (the previous page's `next_after_seq`).

StatusQuery.description: `status` (SPEC §8): the steps view, or with `view: units` one compact row per unit.

brief.description: Cut every string over 200 characters in inputs and outputs (steps view only).

all.description: Include the done units, which are otherwise left out and counted in `done_units`.

state.description: Keep only the units in these states (units view only).

UnitState.description:
A unit's state in the units view, checked in this order (the status table's, `shown`: a
stopped step first): a step failed or stale, a step running, every step succeeded or
skipped, nothing startable and something held, a step queued on resources, else pending.

oneOf.description: The retired message_post's reply, kept for the binaries that sent it.

`board_set`'s reply before it carried warnings (it is now `Data` `{rev, warnings}`),
kept so a reply cached by an older release still decodes.

next_cursor.description:

StateEpoch.description:
The project's execution-state witness (`plans.state_epoch`): the writer adds one in every
transaction that changes something an edit's preparation reads besides the plan itself
(input values, step statuses, outputs and results, the project's pause, resource
capacities and leases). Never decreases; progress and messages leave it alone.

RecipeGeneration.description:
The recipe files a project sees, as a token compared for equality only: the first 16 hex
digits of the SHA-256 of the project's and the home's recipe listing (each file's name,
size and modification time). Recipe files change outside sluice, so there is no counter.

FullStep.description: The compact fields, the declaration as written (`spec`) and its references.

PauseValue.description: `true`, `false` or the pause's reason, as a step's `paused` reads.

StepReference.description: A step's reference to a plan input, another step's output, a step or a unit.

kind.description: `binding` or `gate` (`output` is a plan output's, never a step's).

slot.description: `in.<input>` for a binding, `after` for a gate.

ordinal.description: The index in a fan-in list or in `after`; 0 for a single source.

source_port.description: The output name of a step source; "" for an input, a unit or a step gate.

source_path.description: The `.field` path after the source, without its leading dot; "" for none.

CompactStep.description: A step in a few fields, read from indexed columns without its declaration.

recipe.description: The recipe its unit matches now, if any.

done.description: Every step succeeded or was skipped (SPEC §6.7).

settled.description: No step running and every pending one external or not ready (SPEC §6.7).

next_after_seq.description: The last entry's seq when more entries match, for `after_seq`; null on the last page.

HistoryRecord.description:
The records `plan_history` returns: every plan edit (from `plan_edits`, never trimmed)
and the log's retained `plan.input`, `step.output` and `step.retry` records.

prune_done_after.description:
Retire done units automatically once their last step finished this many seconds ago
(SPEC §6.11); null turns it off, absent leaves it as it is.

prune_keep.description:
Unit-name patterns (`*`, `?`) automatic retiring never removes; `[]` or null clears
them, absent leaves them as they are.

IconUpload.description:
A string is a text icon, or an absolute (or `~/`) path to an image file that the
coordinator reads once; images otherwise cross the broker as bounded data.

BoardSet.description:
`board_set`: set the project's board (an OpenUI Lang program, `docs("board")`) or clear it
with a null `program`. A stale `expected_rev` is a conflict, a program that does not check
is invalid (each bad line listed).

program.description: The board program; null clears the board.

BoardDocRead.description: `board_doc_read`: the board's document, the hand-written part a board's `Doc()` draws.

BoardDocWrite.description:
`board_doc_write`: replace the board's whole document. With `expected_rev`, a document
at another revision is a conflict and nothing changes; the same text again changes nothing.

markdown.description: The whole document, as markdown (at most 64 KiB).

expected_rev.description: The document's revision you read (board_doc_read); refused if it has changed since.

BoardDocEdit.description:
`board_doc_edit`: replace line ranges of the board's document at `expected_rev`, all of
them or none.

expected_rev.description:
The document's revision the line numbers come from (board_doc_read); refused if it
has changed since.

edits.description: The edits, by line numbers of that revision; none may overlap another.

DocEdit.description:
One edit of the board's document: lines `start` to `end` (1-based, inclusive) become
`text`. `end = start - 1` inserts before `start`; `start = lines + 1` appends.

text.description: The new lines (several, or "" to delete the range).

rev.description: The revision the edit was worked out from; another current one is `conflict`.

start.description: `false` adds new steps paused (`"paused": true`) unless they set `paused` themselves.

inputs.description: Recipe step suffix to input name to a literal value.

UnitUpdate.description: `unit_update`: change a unit's member steps by their exact ids.

UnitRemove.description: `unit_remove`: remove every step of a unit.

PlanRead.description: `plan_read`: a page of the plan's steps, in `(position, id)` order.

recipe.description: Only the units this recipe matches (SPEC §6.8's dynamic matching).

subtree.description:
Also every step downstream of the selection: those reading from or gated on
a selected step, transitively.

keep.description:
Unit-name patterns (`*` any run of characters, `?` one) never removed: a selected
unit whose name matches one is kept, `kept` naming the pattern.

StepProgress.description:
Publish a running step's latest values without finishing it, from its current run. Each
field is one of the step's outputs (its fn's or declared) and is checked against its type;
the fields merge over the run's earlier progress. Progress is never final: it feeds no
input, handoff or gate, settles nothing, writes no log record and wakes no wait.

StepSettle.description:
Settle a running step whose run has submitted (it is finishing) on that submission: its
agent is stopped as a cancel stops it, and the step succeeds with the outputs the done
signal would have given it. Only a bare agent fn's step; anything else is refused.

Ask.description:
A question that needs a reply. `to` is a step of the project's current plan,
`orchestrator` or `owner`; the thread and sender are derived, never given.

to.description: Required; a missing or unknown recipient is refused as `invalid`, never stored.

run.description: The asking run: its step is the sender. Without it the caller is the orchestrator.

owner.description: The dashboard speaks as the owner.

Say.description: A note; no reply is expected.

to.description: Required; a missing or unknown recipient is refused as `invalid`, never stored.

Reply.description: A reply to one message: to its sender, on its thread. It resolves an open question.

to_message.description: Select exactly one of this message id or `to`, a sender with one open question.

to.description: Answer this sender's single open question addressed to the caller.

MessagePost.description:
The retired `message_post` wire shape. Only runs started before ask, say and reply
send it; the coordinator translates it and refuses it without a run identity.

owner.description: Read as the owner (the dashboard's identity) instead of the orchestrator.

StepDismiss.description:
The owner sets a cancelled step aside (`dismissed`), or back: a dismissed cancel stays on
its unit but no longer marks its project or holds its unit off the shelf, until the step
is cancelled again. Kept like a read mark (`readers`), never a log record.

LogRead.description:
A page of the log. Every filter narrows only the records it speaks of (an empty list is no
filter): `kinds` every record, `threads` and `recipients` message records, `statuses`
step.status records; a record is kept when every filter that applies to it keeps it.
`threads` without `kinds` also keeps messages only.

statuses.description: Only step.status records whose `to` is one of these.

recipients.description: Only message records whose `to` is one of these (a step id, `orchestrator`, `owner`).

StepWait.description:
`step_wait`: wait until every selected step's status meets `until`, or `timeout_seconds`
pass. Exactly one of `steps` and `tags` selects.

until.description:
`"succeeded"`, `"settled"` or `{"any_of": [statuses]}`. The coordinator checks it and
refuses a bad one as `invalid`.

StepWaitUntil.description:
What `step_wait` waits for: every selected step succeeded, every one settled (§7.1), or
every one in one of the listed statuses.

PlanHistoryQuery.description: `plan_history`: a page of the plan's history, oldest first.

after_seq.description: Only records whose `seq` is greater (the previous page's `next_after_seq`).

StatusQuery.description: `status` (SPEC §8): the steps view, or with `view: units` one compact row per unit.

brief.description: Cut every string over 200 characters in inputs and outputs (steps view only).

all.description: Include the done units, which are otherwise left out and counted in `done_units`.

state.description: Keep only the units in these states (units view only).

UnitState.description:
A unit's state in the units view, checked in this order (the status table's, `shown`: a
stopped step first): a step failed or stale, a step running, every step succeeded or
skipped, nothing startable and something held, a step queued on resources, else pending.

oneOf.description: The retired message_post's reply, kept for the binaries that sent it.

`board_set`'s reply before it carried warnings (it is now `Data` `{rev, warnings}`),
kept so a reply cached by an older release still decodes.

ProjectSummary.description:
One live project as `projects_list` reports it. `settings_rev` is what
`project_update` and `project_delete` take as `expected_settings_rev`.

counts.description: Step status to the number of the plan's steps in it.

board_rev.description: The board's revision: 0 until a board is first set, then one more per set or clear.

resources.description: Each declared resource: `{"capacity": n}` or `{"capacity_fn": fn}`.

slot.description: `in.<input>` for a binding, `after` for a gate.

ordinal.description: The index in a fan-in list or in `after`; 0 for a single source.

source_port.description: The output name of a step source; "" for an input, a unit or a step gate.

source_path.description: The `.field` path after the source, without its leading dot; "" for none.

CompactStep.description: A step in a few fields, read from indexed columns without its declaration.

recipe.description: The recipe its unit matches now, if any.

done.description: Every step succeeded or was skipped (SPEC §6.7).

settled.description: No step running and every pending one external or not ready (SPEC §6.7).

next_after_seq.description: The last entry's seq when more entries match, for `after_seq`; null on the last page.

HistoryRecord.description:
The records `plan_history` returns: every plan edit (from `plan_edits`, never trimmed)
and the log's retained `plan.input`, `step.output` and `step.retry` records.

oneOf.description:
The `plan.edit` record's fields (record payload version 2): the change set replaces the
RFC 6902 `ops`. The `plan_edits` row stores the same `changes`.

PlanChange.description:
One resolved row change, as `plan_edits.changes`, a `plan.edit` record and an edit
preview carry it. A revision's changes are a set (at most one per collection and key),
listed header first, then deletes (inputs, outputs, steps), then puts (inputs, outputs,
steps), each group in key order for deletes and position order for puts.

RootSection.description: A root section of the plan document, in the order `plans.root_order` keeps.

EditResult.description: Every edit tool's reply (with `dry_run`, the preview alone).

rev.description:
The new revision, or the current one when the edit changed nothing (its
`preview.changes` is then empty and nothing was committed).

steps.description: The steps the edit was about (see the tool).

EditPreview.description: An edit's preview: the row changes it makes and what they do to the steps.

would_start.description:
Ready executable steps (never `core.external`), including those in `would_queue`:
within `scope`.

PreviewScope.description:
What an edit's preview describes: the edited steps and what the edit changes for others
(`impact`, the default), or every ready step of the plan (`all`, only with `dry_run`).

BoardView.description: A project's board as `board_get` reads it: no program while none is set.

Message.description:
One message. `to_message` and `answer` are a reply's; `state` and `answered_by`
are a question's as read now (never in the log record). Rows stored before the
verbs existed read with the verb derived from them.

A step's work ended (its agent exited or stopped) without a valid `step_submit`
of the outputs it must submit.

StepWaitResult.description:
`step_wait`'s reply: whether the condition held, each selected step's status (plan order)
and the project log's last seq at that reading, for a `log_read` from there.

oneOf.description: The retired message_post's reply, kept for the binaries that sent it.

`board_set`'s reply before it carried warnings (it is now `Data` `{rev, warnings}`),
kept so a reply cached by an older release still decodes.

ProjectSummary.description:
One live project as `projects_list` reports it. `settings_rev` is what
`project_update` and `project_delete` take as `expected_settings_rev`.

counts.description: Step status to the number of the plan's steps in it.

board_rev.description: The board's revision: 0 until a board is first set, then one more per set or clear.

resources.description: Each declared resource: `{"capacity": n}` or `{"capacity_fn": fn}`.

JsonMap.description: Insertion-ordered object. Decode external requests through `decode_json`.

PlanGetResult.description: `plan_get`: the whole plan, assembled from its rows.

next_cursor.description:
Pass it back as `cursor` with the same project and filters for the next page; null on
the last page.

StateEpoch.description:
The project's execution-state witness (`plans.state_epoch`): the writer adds one in every
transaction that changes something an edit's preparation reads besides the plan itself
(input values, step statuses, outputs and results, the project's pause, resource
capacities and leases). Never decreases; progress and messages leave it alone.

RecipeGeneration.description:
The recipe files a project sees, as a token compared for equality only: the first 16 hex
digits of the SHA-256 of the project's and the home's recipe listing (each file's name,
size and modification time). Recipe files change outside sluice, so there is no counter.

FullStep.description: The compact fields, the declaration as written (`spec`) and its references.

PauseValue.description: `true`, `false` or the pause's reason, as a step's `paused` reads.

The step will run, and its next run is assigned it.
The step has no live or upcoming run; a later run (e.g. a retry) gets it.

Say.title: Say
Say.description: A note; no reply is expected.

to.description: Required; a missing or unknown recipient is refused as `invalid`, never stored.

MessageReceipt.title: MessageReceipt
MessageReceipt.description: What ask, say and reply return.

Delivery.description: How a message reached its recipient when it was posted.

The step has no live or upcoming run; a later run (e.g. a retry) gets it.

Reply.title: Reply
Reply.description: A reply to one message: to its sender, on its thread. It resolves an open question.

to_message.description: Select exactly one of this message id or `to`, a sender with one open question.

to.description: Answer this sender's single open question addressed to the caller.

JsonMap.description: Insertion-ordered object. Decode external requests through `decode_json`.

Ask.title: Ask
Ask.description:
A question that needs a reply. `to` is a step of the project's current plan,
`orchestrator` or `owner`; the thread and sender are derived, never given.

to.description: Required; a missing or unknown recipient is refused as `invalid`, never stored.

run.description: The asking run: its step is the sender. Without it the caller is the orchestrator.

owner.description: The dashboard speaks as the owner.

BoardSet.title: BoardSet
BoardSet.description:
`board_set`: set the project's board (an OpenUI Lang program, `docs("board")`) or clear it
with a null `program`. A stale `expected_rev` is a conflict, a program that does not check
is invalid (each bad line listed).

program.description: The board program; null clears the board.

BoardDocRead.title: BoardDocRead
BoardDocRead.description: `board_doc_read`: the board's document, the hand-written part a board's `Doc()` draws.

BoardDocWrite.title: BoardDocWrite
BoardDocWrite.description:
`board_doc_write`: replace the board's whole document. With `expected_rev`, a document
at another revision is a conflict and nothing changes; the same text again changes nothing.

markdown.description: The whole document, as markdown (at most 64 KiB).

expected_rev.description: The document's revision you read (board_doc_read); refused if it has changed since.

BoardDocEdit.title: BoardDocEdit
BoardDocEdit.description:
`board_doc_edit`: replace line ranges of the board's document at `expected_rev`, all of
them or none.

expected_rev.description:
The document's revision the line numbers come from (board_doc_read); refused if it
has changed since.

edits.description: The edits, by line numbers of that revision; none may overlap another.

DocEdit.description:
One edit of the board's document: lines `start` to `end` (1-based, inclusive) become
`text`. `end = start - 1` inserts before `start`; `start = lines + 1` appends.

text.description: The new lines (several, or "" to delete the range).

DocEdit.title: DocEdit
DocEdit.description:
One edit of the board's document: lines `start` to `end` (1-based, inclusive) become
`text`. `end = start - 1` inserts before `start`; `start = lines + 1` appends.

text.description: The new lines (several, or "" to delete the range).

BoardView.title: BoardView
BoardView.description: A project's board as `board_get` reads it: no program while none is set.

StepWait.title: StepWait
StepWait.description:
`step_wait`: wait until every selected step's status meets `until`, or `timeout_seconds`
pass. Exactly one of `steps` and `tags` selects.

until.description:
`"succeeded"`, `"settled"` or `{"any_of": [statuses]}`. The coordinator checks it and
refuses a bad one as `invalid`.

StepWaitUntil.description:
What `step_wait` waits for: every selected step succeeded, every one settled (§7.1), or
every one in one of the listed statuses.

StepWaitUntil.title: StepWaitUntil
StepWaitUntil.description:
What `step_wait` waits for: every selected step succeeded, every one settled (§7.1), or
every one in one of the listed statuses.

StepWaitResult.title: StepWaitResult
StepWaitResult.description:
`step_wait`'s reply: whether the condition held, each selected step's status (plan order)
and the project log's last seq at that reading, for a `log_read` from there.
